verdict.reasoning: Patient reports fever for about 7 days with feeling “really hot and sweaty all the time,” “sweating during the night,” feeling “quite cold,” muscle aches, nausea, reduced intake, and being “quite tired and unwell.”
Patient says she has been taking ibuprofen and paracetamol “just been taking the recommended dose every day” and that it “does take the edge off a bit,” indicating partial relief.

She denies cough/cold/sore throat: “Mmm, not those sort of symptoms, really”; denies ear pain: “my ears are fine”; denies diarrhoea, neck stiffness, rash, and swollen/tender joints: “not really”; these collectively support absence of listed localizing symptoms.

She describes headaches as longstanding: “something that I've struggled with through years really, just related to screen use, or… changes in weather patterns… high pressure days,” and says “Not more than usual,” indicating no acute change.

She denies urinary symptoms: “there's been no problems there,” “Any painful urination at all? Patient: Uh, not at all, no,” and “Are you passing urine more often than normal? Patient: I don't think so, no it's been fairly regular.”

She states: “I went to Vietnam. Uh, I came back four weeks ago now… we toured… several different parts of the country, and uh, the countryside and some cities as well… we were sort of trekking and, um, cycling, uh, through the farmland.”

Regarding malaria prophylaxis: she confirms she took it, thinks it was a daily tablet, and notes an additional tablet: “I did, yes… I think it was daily… I think it was, uh another one that I took on top of the first one,” and cannot recall the name, so regimen details are unclear.

She reports chronic back pain and physiotherapy: “I often have problems with back pain… I'm under a physiotherapist at the moment,” with diagnosis “related to long periods of time sitting at a desk, and just, uh, bad posture.”
Family history: “My, my father passed away of [heart attack]… Um, sixty eight, I think. Yeah.” This supports MI around age 68.
She reports: “Uh, just Seroxat” as regular medication and separately that she is taking “ibuprofen and paracetamol… from over the counter,” so current meds include all three.
On allergies: “No, I've just really pollen allergy. That's all I have.” Doctor clarifies “OK, so hay fever.” Patient: “Yes, yeah, just hay fever.”
She says she works as a nurse and is vaccinated: “I work as a nurse.” Doctor: “you're up to date with all the vaccinations, Hepatitis B, and that kind of thing?” Patient: “Yes, indeed. Yeah.”
She states: “No, I'm not” to smoking, “Mmm, moderate alcohol intake. Yeah, I don't drink too much,” and “I try and do, uh, some moderate physical exercise a few times a week.”
She reports work impact: “I'm really struggling quite a lot at work at the moment. It's been quite difficult, feeling so, uh, tired all the time.”

Transcript describes 7 days of fever with sweats, myalgias (“aching all over… my muscles are really aching”), nausea, and no identified infection focus: doctor notes “there's no apparent reason from what you've told me… if we can't find a focus of infection, then that's… an outstanding question.”

Doctor summarizes: “you've recently come from, uh, Vietnam… you've had exposure to rural areas… we need to think about things like malaria,” and patient had taken malaria prophylaxis but cannot specify: “I did, yes… I can't remember… I think it was daily… another one that I took on top of the first one.”

Back pain is chronic and not described as acutely worse: “I often have problems with back pain” and physiotherapy focused on posture; no suggestion of recent change, supporting stable chronic mechanical back pain.

She notes occupational limitation: “I'm really struggling quite a lot at work at the moment. It's been quite difficult, feeling so, uh, tired all the time,” and doctor advises she should not work until sorted out.

Doctor proposes: “we're gonna need to bring you into one of our clinics… You come into one of our clinics in central London, that's one option… Or… you could actually just attend a local A and E,” implying urgent in-person assessment today.

Doctor: “I'll be asking for something called thick and thin blood films, to check for malaria. And inflammatory markers and things like those… the GP there… can then decide on how urgent the blood tests and things are going to be,” supporting planned post-exam labs including malaria films and other markers as needed.

Doctor: “I will send a message to one of our admin team members asking them to book you in. And if you can ring the number that I leave in your consultation notes… then they'll slot you in,” matching admin booking plus patient call.
Doctor states: “I don't think you can go into work, uh, until we've sorted this out,” indicating patient should remain off work until assessment/diagnosis.

Physiotherapy for back pain is mentioned as current (“I'm under a physiotherapist at the moment”), but no explicit plan is discussed about continuing or not changing it; stating “with no change discussed” is an inferred management decision not explicitly made.
